Reading it

Plan view puts the rear (patio) at the top and the front porch at the bottom, like the drawings; the garage is on the left. Click anything to read what it is: windows and doors carry their A-1 tag, devices their E-1 tag, fixtures and pipes their P-1 tag, radiant loops their R-1 tag. The exterior walls show the siding outside and drywall inside, so turning them off leaves the finished interior. The radiant loops in the slab and the plumbing under it sit below the plan drawing: turn the drawing off to see them.

To point a comment at one thing, pick it and press Comment, or name the sheet and the tag in the chat (A-1 W12, E-1 R12, P-1 WC1, M-1 S3).

A-1 Floor plan

Redrawn from the owner's A-1 and A-5 (Larson House, 6/11/26). Pick a room for its size and finishes.

Notes

  1. One story, 3,185 sq ft heated to the outside faces (2,962 sq ft of rooms between finished faces); two-car garage 982 sq ft; covered front porch 399 sq ft; covered rear patio 325 sq ft.
  2. Walls: 2x6 exterior, 2x4 interior, as drawn. Ceilings 9' except the 4:12 vault over kitchen and living and the 6:12 vaulted patio ceiling (A-2).
  3. Roof: dark standing-seam metal; 6:12 main hips, 8:12 front gables, 2:12 shed over the front porch. Siding: tan vertical board-and-batten, stone veneer on the front garage gable, cedar-tone posts and an entry gable bracket (A-3).
  4. The room sizes printed on A-1 are kept in the schedule beside the measured areas; the plan's areas run a little larger than the measured ones, consistent with measuring to wall centers.
  5. Datum for every sheet in this app: X in feet from the outside of the garage-door wall, Y in feet from the outside of the master bedroom's rear wall.

S-1 Framing

Wall types, rough openings, headers, blocking and the roof truss layout. Walls numbered from 1, exterior first.

  • 57 wall runs
  • 328 lf exterior wall
  • 375 lf interior wall
  • 1,002 studs
  • 7,580 sf wall board
  • 3,010 sf ceiling board
  • 67 roof trusses
  • 2x6 exterior @ 16"
  • 2x4 partition @ 16"
  • 2x6 plate, staggered 2x4 studs (laundry)
  • blocking

Notes

  1. Datum 0,0 (blue target, top left of the drawing): where the outside face of the garage-door wall (X = 0) meets the line of the outside face of the master bedroom's rear wall (Y = 0). It is the rear-left corner of the layout string lines, not a wall corner: set it from those two lines. The grid is 5'-0" each way from it; X runs to the right (toward the bedroom wing), Y toward the front (the porch). Every sheet uses it.
  2. Walls: 2x6 exterior, 2x4 interior (owner, 2026-10-13), drawn at stud depth (5-1/2" and 3-1/2"). Plumbing walls are 2x4 like the rest; where a 3" drain or vent goes through a plate, strap it (IRC R602.6.1).
  3. Laundry sound walls (green, owner 2026-10-13): 2x6 plates with 2x4 studs alternating faces at 12" o.c. (24" o.c. on each face), R-15 batt woven between, no stud touching both faces. They grow 2" into the laundry, so the master bedroom, master closet, mud room, master hall and powder room keep their A-1 sizes; the laundry is 2" smaller each way. D11 needs a 2x6 pocket frame.
  4. Plate height 9'-1 1/8" (PT plate, 104-5/8" precut studs, double top plate) for 9'-0" ceilings. The kitchen and living vault is in the trusses (4:12 scissor bottom chords); no wall runs past the plate.
  5. Headers: with 8' heads there is 7-5/8" between the rough opening and the top plates, so exterior headers are 7-1/4" deep: 2-2x8 up to a 4' opening, LVL above that (the two 9' garage doors and the 8' patio French doors: engineer to confirm, or raise the plate). Interior walls carry no roof: a flat 2x4 header with cripples (IRC R602.7.4).
  6. Roof: trusses at 24" o.c. bearing on the exterior walls (roof framing schedule). The main trusses span front to rear on the A-2 ridge line; a 2-ply girder truss (G1) on the master-wing/kitchen line carries the master wing and garage trusses, so the wall under it is a partition. Hang every partition top plate with slip clips (no nails into the bottom chords) so truss uplift doesn't crack the ceilings.
  7. Door rough openings: leaf + 2" wide, + 2-1/2" tall; pockets 2 x leaf + 1". Window rough openings: unit + 1/2" each way (confirm with the window maker).
  8. Garage separation: 5/8" Type X on the garage side of the walls to the house and on the garage ceiling; D6 is a 20-minute self-closing door.
  9. Recessed manifold cabinets (purple, R-1): MF-3 and MF-4 sit in 2x4 partitions. Each is a framed opening: kings full height, a flat 2x4 header with cripples above, a flat 2x4 sill, and no cripples below it because the loop leaders come up out of the slab in that bay. Bore the bottom plate and sill 7/8" at each port; nothing else goes in the bay (no boxes, cable or pipe).
  10. Blocking (magenta): the bands on the drawing and the blocking schedule; grab-bar blocking at every toilet, tub and shower; vanity tops and mirrors, the washer box, the TV over the fireplace.

Open items

The particulars to settle on this sheet.

  • Manifold cabinet depth: a 2x4 wall gives 3-1/2". Recessed manifold cabinets usually need 3-3/4" to 4-3/4"; pick the manifold and cabinet first. If it needs more, fur that stretch of wall 26 to 2x6 (it bumps 2" into the living room).
  • MF-3: E-1 R41 (bedroom hall, 24") is in the leader bay under the cabinet; E-1 R47 (living, 16") is in the leader bay under the cabinet; E-1 S16 (living, 48") is inside the rough opening or its header (clear at 53" and up); E-1 S19 (bedroom hall, 48") is inside the rough opening or its header (clear at 53" and up); the fireplace insert is 1'-6 1/2" off the other face: keep the cabinet and its tubing out of the insert's clearances and chase (its manual).
  • MF-4: E-1 R48 (living, 16") is in the leader bay under the cabinet; E-1 R51 (living, 8") is in the leader bay under the cabinet; the fireplace insert is 1'-6 1/2" off the other face: keep the cabinet and its tubing out of the insert's clearances and chase (its manual).
  • Datum: confirm the 0,0 layout corner with the surveyor's pins before the forms go in.
  • Window sizes and heights are scaled from the elevations; confirm the window schedule with the supplier before framing.
  • Bedroom 3's only window (W17, 4'x4') scales with a 4'-0" sill: above the 44" egress limit. Lower it or use a casement sized for egress.
  • Interior door heights are not on the plans (8'-0" assumed to match the exterior doors on the elevations).
  • Roof trusses: the layout here is a draft from A-2. The truss maker designs the trusses, the hip and valley sets, the G1 girder and its end posts, and the over-framed 8:12 gables at the entry and office.
  • Heel: 12" energy heel assumed (full R-49 to the wall line); it sets the eave height on the elevations.
  • Fireplace insert: chimney chase framing through the vaulted living ceiling and roof; clearances per the insert's manual.
  • Living room label on A-1 says 17'-4" wide; the walls measure about 20'-5". Framing follows the walls.
  • Foundation (slab assumed: the garage and mechanical floor drains, the radiant slab), thickened footings under G1's end posts and the patio and porch posts, anchor schedule.

Notes

  1. Panel P1, 200A main breaker, 40 spaces, in the garage on the mud room wall beside D6, 60" to centre, 36" clear in front (110.26). It sits next to the mechanical room (boiler, water heater) and the kitchen, the two heaviest groups of circuits. A meter-main outside on the garage's porch-side wall carries the service disconnect (NEC 2023 230.85 emergency disconnect) and feeds P1 with 4-wire 2/0 Al SER (or #2/0 Al in conduit), neutral isolated in P1.
  2. Code basis: NEC 2023 (confirm the edition Powell / Park County enforces). AFCI on every 120V 15A and 20A branch circuit in the house except the bath receptacle circuits and the garage and exterior circuit (210.12); GFCI in baths, kitchen counters and island, dishwasher, disposal, laundry, garage, outdoors, and within 6 ft of any sink (210.8). GFCI protection is by GFCI receptacles (marked G) at a readily accessible first outlet, which also protect what is downstream (the washer, the door openers); only the dishwasher and disposal, whose receptacles sit in cabinets, use dual-function breakers. Tamper-resistant receptacles throughout (406.12).
  3. Positions: every wall device is drawn on the face of the wall it goes in, with its stem to that wall; the schedule gives the wall and the distance from the nearer corner. Ceiling devices give two distances. Final boxes are set to the studs at the owner walk-through.
  4. Mounting heights (standard): receptacles 16" to centre, switches 48", counter and laundry GFCIs 44", vanity GFCIs 40", vanity lights 84", exterior lights 72" or 84".
  5. Switch plan: every light belongs to one switch leg (table below), switched in the room it lights, at the latch side of the door you walk in through. Rooms with two ways in get 3-ways: the master hall, mud room, kitchen, bedroom hall and garage; the living cans have three control points (entry dimmer, 4-way at the patio doors, 3-way at the bedroom hall). A switch tag that appears in several legs is a multi-gang bank, one rocker per leg. On the page, picking a light or switch lights every device on its legs in blue.
  6. Circuit sheets E-1.1 onward show one circuit each with its cable run drawn from P1 through every device in nearest-neighbour order (solid for receptacle and appliance circuits, dashed for lighting). The run is a proposed order, not a required one. E-1.D shows the Cat6 home runs to the media panel.
  7. Kitchen: two 20A small-appliance circuits (11 left counter and the dining walls, 12 island, front counter and pantry, 210.11(C)(1) and 210.52(B)), counter receptacles at 4 ft spacing (210.52(C)); range, refrigerator, dishwasher, disposal and hood each on their own circuit. The island has a receptacle in each end panel on the living side, below the counter edge. Kitchen and living ceilings are vaulted 4:12: sloped-ceiling can trims and a fan downrod sized for the slope.
  8. Lighting circuits by area, whole switch legs only: 29 master suite, master hall, laundry, powder, mud room; 30 kitchen, dining, pantry, mech room, living, entry, coat closet, porch and patio; 31 office, bedroom wing and every smoke and CO alarm (so a tripped alarm circuit shows as dark lights). Garage and garage exterior lights on 32. Each is well under the 1,440 W continuous limit of a 15A circuit at LED design wattages.
  9. Smoke alarms in every bedroom and the office; smoke + CO combination alarms outside each sleeping area (master hall, bedroom hall, entry outside the office). All 120V, interconnected, battery backup (IRC R314, R315; CO because of the attached garage, the wood fireplace and the gas boiler).
  10. Bath exhaust fans 110 CFM with humidity sensing and an integrated LED light: the light switches with the room's other lights, the fan on its own rocker with a timer (14/3 from the bank). Ducted outside in rigid duct.
  11. Mini-splits: each outdoor unit has its own 2-pole circuit and a fused disconnect within sight; the indoor heads are fed from their outdoor unit through the interconnect cable, so they have no circuits of their own. CU-1 (24k, master, dining and living heads) sits in the rear alcove between the master bedroom and the covered patio, and CU-2 (24k, bedrooms 1-3) in the right side yard against the Bath 2 wall, per M-1; breakers are sized from the nominal units until the nameplates are known. A weatherproof GFCI receptacle is within 25 ft of each outdoor unit (210.63).
  12. Radiant (R-1): the wall-hung boiler HS-1, its system circulator and the zone controller share 15A circuit 27 with a service switch at the boiler, and each remote manifold station has a receptacle on 27 for its actuator wiring module (MF-1 laundry, MF-2/MF-G on the garage side of the mud room wall with the garage circulator, MF-3 bedroom hall). The water heater's power vent is on 32. Thermostats are 24V back to the zone controller, not line voltage. The MF-3 cabinet sits below the hall 3-way S at 48".
  13. Low voltage: Cat6 home runs to the media panel on the pantry's mech-room wall (master and living TV boxes, office desk, video doorbell at the front door), powered from circuit 33.

Open items

The particulars to settle on this sheet.

  • Range fuel: the 48" range is drawn electric on a 50A circuit. A gas or dual-fuel range drops that to a 120V receptacle and adds a gas line.
  • Mini-split breakers are sized from M-1's nominal units (two 24k 3-port units, MCA about 20A, on 25A/#10); set them to the nameplate MCA/MOCP of the units bought.
  • Utility service: overhead or underground, and which side of the house the meter goes on. The meter-main is drawn on the garage wall facing the porch end.
  • EV-ready: a 50A NEMA 14-50 receptacle is drawn in the garage. Keep, swap for a hardwired charger, or drop?
  • Mounting heights: standard heights are drawn. Zero Rd used 30" receptacles and 42" switches for accessibility; say if this house should match.
  • Ceiling fans in the master, living, three bedrooms and the patio: keep the fan-rated boxes, or cans instead?
  • Low voltage: TVs in the bedrooms, ceiling Wi-Fi access points, cameras, and whether the media panel should move out of the pantry.

P-1 Plumbing

Fixtures from A-5; one drain tree out the rear wall at 25,0, and group PEX feeds. A first draft for the plumber (slab on grade).

  • 21 fixtures
  • 41 DFU
  • 35.7 WSFU
  • 5 stacks

Notes

  1. Slab on grade assumed (A-5 shows floor drains in the garage and mechanical closet). All drains and supply runs are under the slab or in walls; no water lines in the attic.
  2. One drain tree, every line falling to where the building drain leaves the house at 25,0 (the rear wall line) at an invert of 2'-6 1/2" below the finished floor: a 4" building drain straight out the rear at X 25, a 3" east trunk at Y 26.8 for the kitchen and both east baths, a 3" master bath branch at Y 12, and a 2" line from the garage and mechanical floor drains. 41 DFU in all.
  3. Slopes are the IPC minimums (1/8" per ft at 3" and 4", 1/4" per ft below 3"), worked back from the exit; the shallowest invert is 1'-5 1/2" under the slab.
  4. Under the slab, top down: 4" of concrete; R-1's 5" nub boards with the radiant loops on them (9" to their underside); R-1's 1" feed pairs right under the boards; then P-1 in the base course, each in its own band so nothing crosses at the same depth: cold PEX about 1'-0" down, hot PEX about 1'-1 1/2" down, and every drain below both (crowns no higher than 1'-2 1/2"). Vent legs under the slab leave their drain at its own depth. Rough in, test and backfill the plumbing before the vapor barrier and boards go down; sleeve each line where it comes up through the boards and slab. R-1's tube runs under the fixtures at 6" centres, so each riser that can move (lav and sink drains, the washer box, the PEX stub-ups and group manifolds, CO3) is set a few inches off its fixture to come up between two tubes; the closet flanges, floor and shower drains, tub drains and stacks can't move, and R-1 marks each one where its installer shifts one run over a channel.
  5. Supply: 1" service to a main manifold in the mechanical closet, then one cold and hot pair to each fixture group, in one piece under the slab (no fittings under the slab), to a small manifold in the vanity or wet wall; short 1/2" lines from there to each fixture. 726 ft of PEX in all. 25.3 cold + 10.4 hot WSFU. Hot runs under the slab get R-3 closed-cell insulation (IECC R403.5.3), since they sit below the radiant boards. Pressure-balanced or thermostatic valves at the tubs and showers.
  6. Hot water takes longest at master bath (about 47 s at a lavatory); see open items for a recirculation pump.
  7. Every trap is vented: up the wall behind the fixture and across the attic to its group's 3" stack, which goes through the roof. Wet walls framed 2x6 (see S-1). ADA toilets as drawn: 17-19" bowl height, grab-bar blocking.
  8. Water heater in the mechanical closet with a pan and the T&P and pan drain to the closet floor drain.

Open items

The particulars to settle on this sheet.

  • Confirm the drain leaves at 25,0 (assumed): city sewer or septic, and the invert there. The house needs about 2'-6 1/2" of cover at the wall plus the fall to the main or tank.
  • Water source (city or well) and where it enters; the main manifold is drawn in the mechanical closet.
  • A demand recirculation pump (button or motion sensor at each bath) on the hot side would cut the wait at the far baths to a few seconds; it needs a 1/2" return or the cold line as the return.
  • Water heater fuel and type. A heat-pump water heater needs about 700 cu ft of air or a ducted kit; the 3' x 8' mechanical closet is too small without one. A gas unit needs venting and combustion air.
  • Powder room sink is not drawn on A-5 (one is shown here, assumed).
  • Garage floor drain: sanitary with an interceptor, or to daylight (lot grading).
  • Kitchen island vent method (loop vent vs. AAV) depends on the local code.
  • Fixture models: A-5 tags the drains K-9135 and K-9136; tub, toilet, faucet and valve models still to pick.

M-1 HVAC

Ductless: two cold-climate multi-zone mini-split heat pumps with wall heads; the radiant slab (R-1) carries the heat.

  • 40,299 Btu/h heating
  • 20,637 Btu/h cooling
  • 2 outdoor units
  • 4 tons of mini-split
  • 6 wall heads
  • refrigerant line sets LS#: double line outside in line-hide, single in the attic or a wall
  • condensate (P = pump)
  • CU-1 heads and the rooms they serve
  • CU-2 heads and the rooms they serve
  • outdoor units, disconnects DS#, controllers T#

Notes

  1. Design conditions: Powell, WY (ASHRAE 2009, Cody Muni AWOS (nearest station to Powell), 99.6 % heating / 1 % cooling). Heating -11.4°F, cooling 87.8°F; inside 70°F / 75°F.
  2. No ducts. The radiant slab (R-1) heats every room; the mini-splits cool the rooms with heads and give fast, second-source heat there. Rooms without a head (office, laundry, mud room, powder, halls) take air from the next room through their doors.
  3. Sizing: each head carries the cooling load of the rooms it serves plus 15 % for latent and margin, with 6k the smallest head; the living head is held at 9k for the vault, the open kitchen and cooking. Each outdoor unit is the smallest common cold-climate multi-zone with enough ports, with the heads at no more than 130 % of its rating.
  4. Outdoor units sit on a concrete pad against an exterior wall, raised 12" on a stand for snow, backs 30" off the wall so they are outside the eave drip line and can be serviced; snow guards on the roof above each. CU-1 is in the rear alcove between the master bedroom and the patio; CU-2 is on the Bath 2 wall of the bedroom wing. Line sets were routed for the shortest run from there.
  5. Line sets to heads on exterior walls stay outside: from the unit in a painted line-hide along the wall at about 8' (just above the window heads) and straight through the wall into the back of the head (IU-5, IU-6). The others go through a sealed sleeve about 18" up, rise inside a full-height stud bay to the attic, run on the ceiling framing under the insulation and drop inside the wall behind the head. The living set rides the low edge of the kitchen/living vault at Y 17'-6", where the scissor trusses' bottom chord is only about 6" above the plate, then the Bedroom 1 and hall attics; nothing crosses the middle of the vault.
  6. Heads mount high on the wall, top 6" below the ceiling, on a wall that lets them throw across the room. Exterior-wall heads drain condensate by gravity straight out the wall to a splash block (with the line set where there is one); interior-wall heads (IU-2, IU-3) get a mini condensate pump behind the head that discharges outside with the line set.
  7. Pressure test, evacuate and pull a micron vacuum per the maker. Every sleeve is sealed and flashed; line-hide painted to the siding.
  8. Each outdoor unit has a dedicated 240 V circuit and a fused disconnect on the wall within sight (DS1 on the master bedroom's alcove wall, DS2 beside CU-2 on the Bath 2 wall), sized to the nameplate MCA/MOCP once the units are picked (E-1). The heads are powered from their outdoor unit through the 14/4 interconnect run with the line set.
  9. Wired wall controllers T1-T6 at 48" by each door; set the heads to cool and to heat only below the slab's setpoint so they don't fight the radiant.
  10. Ventilation: with no ducts, the draft assumes continuous low-speed bath fans (exhaust-only, E-1) for the IRC whole-house rate; paired through-wall ERVs are the upgrade (see open items).

Open items

The particulars to settle on this sheet.

  • CU-1 in the rear alcove: it is 2 ft from the edge of the covered patio and under the dining windows, so it is heard on the patio and in the dining room when it runs. The alternatives are the master bedroom's left wall (quiet, but the living set runs about 105 ft, past the per-head limit) or the front porch (every set under 75 ft, in sight of the street).
  • CU-2 on the Bath 2 wall: 3 ft from Bedroom 2's window W14. The Bath 1 wall is the quiet spot (8 ft from any bedroom window) for about 10 ft more line.
  • Exact models: pick the brand, then confirm the heads are an allowed combination and the line lengths are inside the unit's limits (CU-1: longest 69 ft, total 145 ft; CU-2: longest 57 ft, total 102 ft).
  • Truss maker: the living set crosses the scissor trusses at Y 17'-6"; leave web openings for a 2" bundle there, or run it along a truss.
  • Office: no head as drawn (the ask was the right-side bedrooms). A 6k head on the office's right wall would make CU-2 a 4-port.
  • Bed walls: the master and Bedroom 1 heads sit on the rear wall between the windows, where a headboard may go. A head over a headboard works with its vanes set level; otherwise it moves to a side wall. Confirm furniture walls before rough-in.
  • Ventilation: continuous bath fans (drawn) or paired through-wall ERVs (about 133 CFM continuous under the IRC).

R-1 Radiant floor

PEX loops on 3" nub boards under the slab: 200' loops, nothing crossing, five manifolds on four zones with a circulator each, flows at Powell, WY design (-11°F).

  • 44 loops
  • 7,200 ft of 1/2" PEX
  • 5 manifolds
  • 42,610 Btu/h house
  • 53,534 Btu/h with the garage
  • 110 °F supply at design
  • Zone 1, Garage (held at 50°F) (T1)
  • Zone 2, Great room (T2)
  • Zone 3, Master suite and utility (T3)
  • Zone 4, Bedroom wing and office (T4)
  • 1" feed pair from the closet circulators, under the boards

Notes

  1. The layout is drawn on the boards' own grid. EPS25 Super 4 nub boards (4' x 4', 5" thick: 4" of EPS, R-18, under a 1" grid of pucks on 3" centres) go down in a running bond with their puck rows on the 3" lines from the datum at 0,0 (the garage-door wall's outside face and the master bed's rear wall line, as on every sheet), so every tube on this sheet sits in a channel between pucks. Lay the first board's corner at the datum and the rest follow; a board cut at a wall keeps its grid.
  2. Tube: 44 loops of 1/2" O2-barrier PEX, none over 200' with its leaders and the 2' rises at the cabinet (L6 is the longest at 192', L5 the shortest at 116'). Fields at 6" o.c. (every other channel), supply and return side by side so each loop's two ends leave its field together; leaders run as 3" pairs through doorways and along walls to their manifold. Nothing crosses anything: the whole layout was checked tube by tube on the grid. One continuous coil per loop, no fittings in the slab; tag both ends with the loop number at the cabinet. The loops on one manifold are planned to like lengths so they balance on their flow meters (MF-1 116'-192', MF-2 167'-189', MF-3 143'-173', MF-4 136'-181', MF-G 147'-187'); MF-1's spread is the master bath, whose three small fields are boxed in by the toilet and shower walls and can neither join each other nor share rows with the bedroom.
  3. Under a wall only where drawn, straight across and only for the length drawn: under the master bed wall into MF-1, under the kitchen wall into the pantry and under the pantry wall into MF-2, under the living room wall into MF-3 and MF-4, under the master hall wall into the powder room, and under the bath 1 wall from the bedroom 2 closet. Mark every wall crossing on the boards before the pour so the plate anchors and shots stay 12" off it; everywhere else the leaders go through the doorway.
  4. The tube runs under everything that sits on the floor: the kitchen base cabinets, island, fridge and range, the washer and dryer, the tubs, showers, vanities and toilets, the hearth. It lies about 5" below the top of the slab, so nothing fastened to the floor reaches it; only the walls and their plates, the posts and the manifold port rows keep it out. Where P-1 brings a drain, a tub trap, a closet flange or a vent stack up through the slab (15 places, each marked with a crossed circle) shift the one run it meets over a channel for the length of the fitting, so the tube stays 3" clear of the flange or drain body; the showers' floors are heated like the rest.
  5. Manifolds, five stations, each wholly on one zone, each with a 3" port position per tube end in one row along its wall (the schedule gives every loop's two port numbers, counted from the low end of the row): MF-1 (laundry, on the north wall from the linen alcove to the east wall, over the dryer, 9 loops) serves Master Bed, Master Bath, Master Closet, Master Hall, Laundry, Powder, Mud Room; MF-2 (mechanical closet, low on the east wall under HS-1, 6 loops) serves Kitchen, Pantry; MF-3 (bedroom hall, west wall north of the fireplace, 7 loops) serves Living, Entry; MF-4 (bedroom hall, west wall south of the fireplace, 11 loops) serves Office, Bedroom 1, Bath 1, Closet (Bedroom 2), Bedroom 2, Bath 2, Bedroom 3, Closet (Bedroom 3); MF-G (garage, on the mud room wall (two 7-loop manifolds side by side), 11 loops) serves Mechanical, Garage. The four circulators are in the mechanical closet with HS-1: MF-2 is piped to P-R2 there; MF-1, MF-3, MF-4 and MF-G each get a 1" insulated pair under the boards, 162' each way in all.
  6. The leaders rise straight up out of the slab at their port positions into the cabinet (sleeve each rise in 12" of pipe insulation where it leaves the concrete) and bundle up to the manifold; they may be gathered sideways in the last 12" below the cabinet. Cabinets are recessed in the hall wall (MF-3, MF-4) and surface-mounted on the laundry's sound wall (MF-1), low on the closet's east wall under the boiler (MF-2) and on the garage face of the mud room wall (MF-G).
  7. Zoning is by manifold: four zones (garage; great room; master suite and utility; bedroom wing and office), each a circulator in the mechanical closet started by its thermostat, and every loop on a manifold is on that manifold's zone. Zone 2 has two manifolds, MF-2 and MF-3, on the one circulator. No actuators: balance each loop on its flow meter.
  8. Flow: 10.9 gpm with every loop calling, each loop set on its flow meter at a 10°F drop. Design heat 53,534 Btu/h, of which 10,924 is the garage at 50°F; 7% is added for heat lost down through the R-18 boards and out the slab edge. Rooms with no field of their own are heated by the leader bundles running through them: Dining (231' of leaders for 3,771 Btu/h), Bedroom Hall (166' of leaders for 422 Btu/h). Nothing heats the Coat Closet (30 Btu/h), Bedroom 1 Closet (86 Btu/h); they borrow from the rooms around them.
  9. Water: 110°F supply at -11°F outside, reset lower as it warms, so a condensing boiler stays condensing. Floor surfaces stay at or under 100°F. At that supply L31 (Bedroom 3, Closet (Bedroom 3)) falls about 345 Btu/h short at design; see the open items.
  10. Pumps: one constant-ΔP ECM circulator per zone, sized on the zone's hardest loop plus about 3 ft for the feed pair and manifold: P-R1 about 4 ft (L36, 2.3 gpm); P-R2 about 5 ft (L15, 3.1 gpm); P-R3 about 5 ft (L6, 2.2 gpm); P-R4 about 5 ft (L26, 3.4 gpm).
  11. Under the boards: 10-mil vapor barrier over the compacted base, lapped and taped; R-10 (2") rigid foam at the slab edge. The 4" slab goes over the pucks with the tube tops about 1" below the surface of the boards; no mesh ties are needed, the pucks hold the tube. Pressure test every loop at 100 psi water or 60 psi air for 24 hours before the pour and keep it under pressure through the pour. Photograph every room with a tape in frame before concrete.
  12. HS-1, the four circulators and the zone controller are circuit 27 on E-1 (200 A panel in the garage); the manifold cabinets need no power. T1 to T4 wire to the zone controller in the closet.
  13. P-1's water lines, vents and drains are all in the base course below the boards and the feed pairs (cold PEX 1'-0" down, hot 1'-1 1/2", drains below both), so the boards go down whole, with no channels cut for plumbing.

Open items

The particulars to settle on this sheet.

  • L31 (Bedroom 3, Closet (Bedroom 3)): the floor carries all but about 345 Btu/h of the room at -11°F with 110°F water. Add a small electric towel warmer, or run the boiler hotter on the coldest days.
  • Not tubed: the coat closet (about 6 sq ft), the bedroom 1 bypass closet (about 20 sq ft), the 3' x 10' notch at the garage's north wall beside the master closet (about 31 sq ft, left bare by decision 2026-10-14), the laundry's west floor along the counter (about 15 sq ft: every way of tubing it either takes the laundry loop past 200' or crosses the closet and mud room leaders that use that floor) and the west 18" of the powder room under the lav (about 9 sq ft: the powder is the middle panel of the mud room leg's loop, which can only be 3' or 5' wide there, and 5' would not clear the east wall). The first three are too small for a loop of their own at the lengths on their manifold, and none can be added to a neighbouring loop without crossing another. All five sit inside heated floor and borrow from it.
  • Boiler model: HS-1 is a condensing boiler on natural gas or propane (decided 2026-10-13). Pick a combi or a boiler with an indirect tank if it should also make the domestic hot water and replace P-1's 50 gal heater; propane needs the boiler's LP conversion kit.
  • Garage: kept at 50°F on its own manifold, pump and thermostat. Decide whether it runs a glycol mix behind a plate heat exchanger, which protects it if the house loses power in a cold snap with the doors open.
  • Flooring: the loops assume hard-surface floors. Carpet in a bedroom needs about 10°F warmer water for that loop.
  • S-1: MF-3 and MF-4 recess into the hall's 2x4 west wall (3-1/2" deep; fur locally if the chosen manifold needs more). MF-4's recess is 2'-0" longer than S-1 framed it, 32'-0" to 37'-3" along the wall; the MF-K and MF-5 recesses are no longer needed and MF-1's surface cabinet now runs 18'-6" to 24'-3" at 4' up, over the dryer.
  • E-1: no actuators, so the receptacles at the manifold cabinets are not needed; HS-1, the four circulators and the zone controller stay on circuit 27, and T1 to T4 wire to the zone controller in the closet.
  • P-1: the closet's east wall is shared, MF-2 low at its north end under HS-1 and the water heater at its south end; the main water manifold and its risers stay west of MF-2's port column (x 33'-6"). The pantry floor carries MF-2's leaders at 3" across its west end and runs warmer than the rooms around it; sleeve the bundle if the pantry should stay cool.
  • The EPS25 Super 4 nub boards come 5 to a bundle (80 sq ft), 3 bundles minimum: 55 bundles cover the 4,167 sq ft slab with 5% for cuts. Confirm the lead time; the board layout can start at any corner as long as the grid holds the datum.
